newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-BHP Petroleum profit surges 69 pct.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-BHP Petroleum profit surges 69 pct.

text.p: The Broken Hill Proprietary Co Ltd said on Friday that profit from its petroleum division had increased 69.2 percent to A$335 million when abnormal items were excluded.

The company cited a higher average realised oil price, higher sales volumes for both oil and condensate, improved product margins from its Hawaii refinery and the elimination of depreciation expenses for the Dai Hung project in Vietnam.

Profit for the half year including abnormals was 123.2 percent higher at A$442 million. An abnormal profit of A$107 million was booked after settlement of the resources rent tax dispute with the Victorian government.
Average realised oil prices for the six months rose to A$27.60 from A$23.35, reflecting higher US dollars prices partly offset by a stronger Australian dollar, the company said.
Net profits from asset sales in Argentina of A$56 million and in the UK of A$50 million were partly offset by a write-down of A$24 million on its Wyoming assets in the US.

On a quarterly basis, however, profit excluding abnormals for the November 1996 quarter dropped 23 percent to A$146 million when compared to the August 1996 quarter, with the company citing higher exploration expenses and the Wyoming asset write-down.
BHP said oil and condensate production rose three percent due to the commencement of production from the Cossack/Wanaea field offshore Western Australia and the Liverpool Bay field in the UK.

Natural gas production fell four percent due to the sale of US producing assets and lower Bass Strait demand, partly offset by the commencement of Liverpool Bay and and higher UK demand, the company said.
By 12.25 p.m. (0120 GMT), BHP shares were 17 cents higher at A$17.22 after earlier hitting a high of A$17.59.
